description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROPE—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy in percentage from 60% to 80%. The Base method, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 61.5% and increases steadily to about 66.5% as the co-occurrence number grows. The MEND method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, begins at around 65.5% and rises to approximately 74%, showing a consistent upward trend. The FT method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 62.5% and increases to roughly 68.5%, also showing a steady rise. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line with diamond markers, begins at approximately 66.5% and increases to about 72.5%, following a similar upward trend. The ROPE method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 72.5% and increases to approximately 77.5%, maintaining the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers. All methods show an increase in accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers, with ROPE consistently outperforming the others.
